mcat_description.short: A greenhouse (polyhouse) is a prefabricated protected cultivation structure with a GI or MS tubular frame covered by UV-stabilised polyethylene film, polycarbonate panels, or glass, sold as a complete turnkey structure or in component kits to farmers and agri-entrepreneurs for year-round crop production.
mcat_description.long: Greenhouses in India are primarily GI-framed polyhouses covered with UV-stabilised polyethylene film, used for protected cultivation of vegetables, cut flowers, and high-value horticultural crops under controlled temperature and humidity conditions. Structures are classified by ventilation type (naturally ventilated, fan-and-pad), glazing material (polyethylene film, polycarbonate panels, glass), and structural form (Quonset/tunnel, even-span, sawtooth, multi-span/gutter-connected). The Indian market is strongly shaped by NHB and MIDH subsidy norms, which specify minimum technical standards including IS 15827:2009 for polyhouse film and minimum 200-micron UV-stabilised polythene. Buyers range from small farmers seeking low-cost naturally ventilated structures to commercial horticulture enterprises requiring hi-tech fan-and-pad climate-controlled systems.

market_context: In India, 'greenhouse' and 'polyhouse' are used interchangeably in trade vocabulary, with polyhouse being the dominant commercial term for GI-framed structures covered with UV-stabilised polyethylene film. The market is strongly structured by government subsidy schemes — NHB (National Horticulture Board) and MIDH (Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture) — which define technical specifications including IS 15827:2009 for polyhouse film and minimum 200-micron UV-stabilised polythene cover. Naturally ventilated polyhouses and fan-and-pad (hi-tech) greenhouses are the two primary commercial categories; shade net houses are a lower-cost adjacent category. Polycarbonate greenhouses are a growing premium segment, particularly for hilly/cold regions where polyethylene film performs poorly. Glass greenhouses remain a niche, high-investment segment. Key structural forms in India include Quonset/tunnel (most economical), multi-span/gutter-connected (large commercial farms), sawtooth (cut flower production), and even-span. Agriplast Tech India is a notable Indian manufacturer; regional suppliers are concentrated in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat, and Rajasthan. Keyword data shows a notable niche demand for saffron indoor farming setups, reflecting emerging controlled-environment agriculture beyond traditional horticulture.
